In a gravity framework with a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE) (the 1/2 fitted), each galaxy's extra lensing mass is a collisionless 'cold' component settling onto the law g_N = g^2/(g + a0).
(3) N = 1/f_ret from the baryon census used in the framework's simulations (N ~ 6-10) fits within 0.31 Mpc with no fitted parameter (-0.2 / -1.5);

Limits: the absolute fit is poor for every model including the plain law (chi^2 ~160/52), concentrated in the most massive bins (the known massive/early-type excess); the census supply is an observational input (a framework derivation failed); the two-halo simulation uses inherited initial conditions; one sigma_8 cross-check failed by 3.2%.

records.delta: The cold halo has no edge: truncating each galaxy at its cosmic cold share is excluded at Delta chi^2 +197 (+753 all radii), while the framework's own infall onto the law fits as well as an edgeless law if each galaxy draws N >= 3-4 times its baryons, and the census value N ~ 6-10 fits with no free parameter.
records.fingerprint: truncation excluded at Delta chi^2 +197 within 0.31 Mpc, +753 all radii; N ~ 6-10 fits at -0.2/-1.5
records.test: KiDS-1000 isolated-galaxy lensing beyond 0.31 Mpc: the two-halo term narrows the outer deficit from +149 to +11 (effective bias 0.2-0.5), so the shape of the profile at 0.3-1 Mpc is the discriminator.

records.title: Where a Dark-Energy-Tied Galaxy Law Holds and Where It Breaks: Low-Acceleration Tests, a Two-Footing Shear Pass, and the Satellite-Dwarf Excess (Working Note)

claims.quote: (2) Isolated late-type galaxies obey the law down to g_bar ~ 7e-14 m/s^2 in KiDS-1000 lensing (amplitude 1.016 +/- 0.086; within ~0.1 dex across robustness variants), excluding the satellite dwarfs' x2.75 at >= 12 sigma in every variant.

One day of pre-registered tests (frozen criteria before computing, mutation controls, both a0 footings never pooled) of a gravity framework with galactic law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE), whose extra gravitating mass is a collisionless 'cold energy' component.
(3) Spheroidal/red isolated lenses sit 1.45x above the law at the same accelerations after a stellar-mass correction (4.0 sigma split) and follow g_obs = g_law (g_dagger/g_bar)^0.060;

(4) Lensing equals dynamics in the framework to better than 2e-5; in the candidate particle model a uniform field produces no internal response, so the law's cold mass must be real mass assembled from afar; a conditional confinement theorem for the two-population cold medium is stated.

records.delta: The law is confirmed at the lowest acceleration ever tested (7e-14 m/s^2, amplitude 1.016 +- 0.086) and fails only where the mass is pressure-supported: spheroidal lenses sit 1.45x above it (4.0 sigma) and satellite dwarfs +0.44 dex, and ten framework-native mechanisms fail to produce the dwarf excess. This is the sharpest statement of the theory's central anomaly.
records.fingerprint: law holds to g_bar ~ 7e-14 m/s^2, amplitude 1.016 +- 0.086; spheroidals 1.45x above at 4.0 sigma; dwarfs +0.44 dex
records.test: A kinematic selector that separates rotating from pressure-supported systems at fixed g_bar: five candidates already fail, so the test is a new one (e.g. velocity-dispersion-weighted shape) applied to the same isolated-lens sample.

records.title: Why Cold Energy Settles: A Tethered Medium Whose Displacement Is the Gravitational Polarization (Working Note)

claims.quote: Correction (v1.1; wording fixed in v1.2): the exact static solution needs negative cold-energy density in a thin pancake through the saddle between two bodies (-89 times the mean cold density at R = 0.2 d for a Milky-Way-M31-like pair, -33 for a cluster pair, canonical footing).

Under the law the column through the saddle drops almost to zero in a narrow band; a positive medium cannot dig the part below zero density, a missing depth of 1.9 to 2.1 Msun/pc^2 (Milky-Way-M31-like pair) and 4.6 to 5.1 Msun/pc^2 (cluster pair).
With K = 4 pi G and u = K|P|, the action is L = -|grad Phi - K P|^2/(2K) - rho_b Phi - W_rem(u) - (gamma/2)|grad P|^2, with K dW_rem/du = u^2/(a0 - u) and gamma = K L*^2/2.
It screens the Solar System: Cassini's quadrupole is at most 5e-8 of the 2026 bound and the only residue is a uniform sunward pull of at most 2.4e-16 m/s^2.

Sealed kill lines: a Cavendish test at four times the source acceleration (|dG/G| < 1e-6), a probe beyond 1000 AU (no non-thermal anomaly at or above 1e-13 m/s^2), and Gaia DR4 wide binaries (Newtonian).

records.delta: The tether is a positive-mass medium, so it cannot reproduce MOND's negative phantom density near field null points: the exact static solution needs -89 rho_bar in a thin pancake, and the framework therefore predicts NO saddle dip where QUMOND predicts one - a kill test that separates the two.
records.fingerprint: L* between 24 pc and about 1 kpc; missing saddle depth 1.9 to 2.1 Msun/pc^2
records.test: Stacked lensing of luminous-red-galaxy pairs at the 0.77 Mpc separation: the missing depth is 1.9-2.1 Msun/pc^2 and needs about twelve times the pairs of arXiv:1702.08485 for 3 sigma.
